test: Local solo race frame timing before presentation interpolation changes

scope.browser: Installed Google Chrome, headless, separate Playwright browser
scope.instrumentation: Measured the application frame callback and requestAnimationFrame intervals; Chrome CPU sampling at 1 ms; PerformanceObserver long-task records

assessment: No local CPU frame-budget bottleneck or long task appeared in this sample.
Solo simulation positions were presented at 30 Hz without pose interpolation, which can produce motion jitter despite a 60 Hz renderer.
Camera lane smoothing adds perceived steering latency; toast overlays could intercept action-button clicks.
No SnapshotBuffer correctness defect was demonstrated. Its 95 ms multiplayer interpolation buffer remains unchanged; adaptive buffering needs measured network-jitter evidence.
limitations: This short headless desktop sample is not a physical Peloton performance measurement.
No real microphone, bike sensor, remote server, internet latency, or Wi-Fi jitter was measured.
Timing instrumentation adds small overhead, and concurrently running development tasks may influence results.
The hardware model and Chrome version were not recorded; results are evidence for this local sample, not a device guarantee.
